subtitle: Lesson 26 · Wait Statistics & Bottleneck Analysis

eyebrow: The three core I/O wait types
code:
PAGEIOLATCH_SH   page read for shared access
PAGEIOLATCH_EX   page read for exclusive access
WRITELOG         log write hardening to disk
IO_COMPLETION    other non-buffer-pool I/O

SELECT wait_type, wait_time_ms, signal_wait_time_ms
FROM sys.dm_os_wait_stats
WHERE wait_type IN
  ('PAGEIOLATCH_SH','PAGEIOLATCH_EX',
   'WRITELOG','IO_COMPLETION');
caption: PAGEIOLATCH points at data files. WRITELOG points at the log.

eyebrow: Which physical file is actually stalling
code:
SELECT DB_NAME(vfs.database_id) AS db,
    mf.physical_name,
    vfs.io_stall_read_ms, vfs.io_stall_write_ms,
    vfs.io_stall_read_ms /
        NULLIF(vfs.num_of_reads, 0) AS avg_read_ms
FROM sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats(NULL, NULL) vfs
JOIN sys.master_files mf
    ON vfs.database_id = mf.database_id
    AND vfs.file_id = mf.file_id
ORDER BY vfs.io_stall_read_ms
       + vfs.io_stall_write_ms DESC;
caption: Low single-digit ms average is healthy; tens of ms is worth escalating.
